title: Identifiability Degree of Direct Effects in Polytrees with Correlated Errors and Colliders
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted: the promised all-branch randomized FPT classifier remains open while the delivered result is a structural degree theorem with a repairable residual-case gap.
gap_reasons: The promised all-branch randomized 2^{O(c)} poly(n,L,log(1/delta)) classifier is left open; the current kernel delivers the degree/classification theorem but not the headlined algorithmic object.

The claimed exhaustion omits root--indegree-one forbidden residual equations, which are affine constraints (and can pin or contradict a scalar coefficient), so the quadratic-core reconstruction is not established.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed a collider-parameterized quadratic-core and coordinate-degree argument, with an exact one-collider quartic witness. D0.5 found that the commissioned all-branch randomized fixed-parameter classifier was left as an open question, and that the quadratic-core proof omitted root--indegree-one residual equations. The latter has a local repair, but the algorithmic theorem still requires new chart, identity-test, intermediate-degree, certificate, and bit-complexity arguments; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: Correlated errors turn direct-effect recovery into an algebraic fiber problem. For acyclic orientations of a connected tree with maximum indegree two, the proved reduction preserves every coordinate branch in a quadratic core with at most \(2c\) collider variables, and the proved trichotomy classifies each directed coefficient as rational, finitely algebraic, or varying on a positive-dimensional component, with degree at most \(\max\{2,4^c\}\). An exact seven-vertex example attains degree four when \(c=1\), and positive-definite specializations exhibit two and four real joint lifts. Attainment or asymptotic tightness of \(4^c\) for connected polytrees with \(c\ge2\), the intermediate degree spectrum, and a uniform \(2^{O(c)}\operatorname{poly}(n,L)\) randomized bit-time classifier remain open.
gap: GuptaBlaser2024 and BriefsBlaser2025 solve rooted directed trees because every nonroot residual contains one coefficient; general graphical criteria and polynomial-space algorithms give no collider-parameter degree or runtime.
fill: The project targets complete localized reconstruction to a \(2c\)-variable quadratic core, a sharp \(4^c\) coordinate bound, exact separation of complex and real branches, and the intermediate-degree obligations for a fixed-parameter classifier.
